summary: Codemasters toy-scale racing series based on the Galoob/Micro Machines toy line, known for household tracks, shared-screen multiplayer, J-Cart support, and later 3D and online revivals.

entries.title: Micro Machines

emulation.emulator: Genesis Plus GX / Mesen / WinUAE / DOSBox / SameBoy / ares
emulation.notes: Use Genesis emulation for the primary route; other emulators cover alternate ports.

primary.why: The original Micro Machines was ported across 8-bit, 16-bit, computer, and CD-i platforms. The Mega Drive/Genesis version is the strongest main route for the classic 16-bit presentation and remains one of the best-regarded versions, while the other ports are preservation alternatives.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Mega Drive/Genesis version in a modern Genesis emulator; use NES, computer, handheld, and SNES ports only for comparison or platform-specific nostalgia.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2002 reboot and 2016 free-to-play revival are separate entries, not replacements for the 1991 original.

entries.title: Micro Machines 2: Turbo Tournament
entries.definitive_edition: Micro Machines Turbo Tournament '96 plus MS-DOS editor secondary

emulation.emulator: Genesis Plus GX / DOSBox / SameBoy / bsnes
emulation.notes: Use Genesis emulation for the primary and DOSBox for the editor secondary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: 16-bit J-Cart multiplayer emulation plus DOS editor

primary.why: Micro Machines 2 added vehicles, modes, and J-Cart multiplayer. The PAL Mega Drive Turbo Tournament '96 update adds new tracks, a track construction kit, and a new soundtrack while preserving the J-Cart party-play strength, making it the best main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Micro Machines Turbo Tournament '96 in a Mega Drive/Genesis emulator with multitap/controller-sharing configured; use MS-DOS for PC track-editor comparison.

secondary.exclusive_content: PC track editor with custom vehicles, backgrounds, obstacles, and import/export support.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the MS-DOS version specifically for its PC editor workflow.
secondary.why: The DOS version has sourced editor features that are different enough to preserve as a secondary creation route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Turbo Tournament '96 was a PAL Mega Drive update rather than a full modern remaster.

entries.title: Micro Machines Military

emulation.notes: Use PAL region settings and configure multiplayer/controller sharing if needed.

primary.why: Micro Machines Military was released only as a PAL Mega Drive J-Cart and adds military vehicles, weapons, and new tracks, so the Mega Drive route is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PAL Mega Drive release in a Genesis emulator with the correct region and multiplayer setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or later port is sourced.

entries.title: Micro Machines V3

emulation.notes: Use Windows as primary; emulate PlayStation/N64/GBC only for comparison.

primary.why: Micro Machines V3 brought the series into 3D and released on PlayStation, Windows, Nintendo 64, and Game Boy Color. The Windows version has the highest output ceiling among the 3D releases, while the Game Boy Color version is a separate 2D handheld adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility setup; use PlayStation or Nintendo 64 emulation as console fallbacks.

entries.remaster_caveats: A Sega Saturn version was demonstrated but not released.

emulation.notes: Use PlayStation emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Micro Maniacs is a Micro Machines spin-off with tiny racing characters instead of vehicles and released for PlayStation and Game Boy Color. The PlayStation version is the higher-fidelity main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version in DuckStation; use Game Boy Color only for handheld comparison.

entries.title: Micro Machines

emulation.notes: Use Xbox as primary; PS2 and GameCube are fallback console routes.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output via hardware or emulation

primary.why: The 2002 Micro Machines reboot released for PlayStation 2, GameCube, Xbox, and Game Boy Advance. The Xbox version has the highest console hardware ceiling among the sourced versions, while the handheld version is a lower-fidelity adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox release on original hardware or xemu; use PlayStation 2/GameCube emulation as fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a reboot, not the 1991 original; regional cancellations affected the GameCube and Xbox versions in the United States.

emulation.notes: Use Windows as primary; PS2/PSP/DS are fallback or comparison routes.

primary.why: Micro Machines V4 released on Windows, PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, and Nintendo DS. The Windows release has the highest output ceiling and the track editor, while the PSP and DS versions are sourced as lacking the editor.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatibility setup; use PS2 only as a console fallback and handheld versions only for portable comparison.

entries.title: Micro Machines
entries.definitive_edition: iOS launch release, preservation-only after shutdown

emulation.emulator: Original iOS/Android hardware or preserved mobile environment
emulation.notes: No live official route is sourced after server retirement.

primary.why: The 2016 Micro Machines revival launched first on iOS and later on Android and Remix OS, but its servers were retired in August 2018 after server and coding issues. iOS is the historical primary route, though modern play depends on preservation rather than live service access.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved iOS software/hardware where available; expect official online service features to be unavailable after the 2018 shutdown.

entries.remaster_caveats: Servers were retired in August 2018, so this entry is primarily archival.

entries.title: Micro Machines World Series
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release, offline/local only after server shutdown

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output, online-limited after server shutdown

primary.why: Micro Machines World Series released for Windows, OS X, Linux, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. Windows has the highest scalable fidelity ceiling, though the online servers were shut down on March 21, 2024.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release for local/offline-supported content where available; do not expect official online server features after March 21, 2024.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online services are shut down, so the current recommendation is limited to remaining offline/local content.
